- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a spike (e.g., +5%+ above mean); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- Model shows persistent lag in price recovery after sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, forecast should rise 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model is 2–3% above true mean for 5+ days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses 1–2% in the final 5–7 days; apply a “tail correction” of +0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
